results.title: Irreducible complex matrix representations (Kourovka 16.67)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a natural number. A homomorphism $\rho \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ is irreducible when $n \ge 1$ and every subspace $W$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that $\rho(g) v \in W$ for all $g \in G$ and all $v \in W$ is either $0$ or $\mathbb{C}^n$.

results.title: Equivalent complex matrix representations (Kourovka 16.67)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a natural number. Two homomorphisms $\rho, \sigma \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ are equivalent when there is a single invertible matrix $P \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ with $\sigma(g) = P \rho(g) P^{-1}$ for every $g \in G$.

results.title: Moretó's conjecture on equal character degrees of symmetric groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every natural number $k$ there is a natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$ there are a natural number $d$ and irreducible representations $\rho_1, \dots, \rho_k$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ into $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{C})$ that are pairwise inequivalent: $\rho_i$ and $\rho_j$ are not equivalent whenever $i \ne j$.

results.title: Symmetric groups have many irreducible characters of equal degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Moretó's conjecture holds: for every natural number $k$ there is a natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$ there are a natural number $d$ and irreducible representations $\rho_1, \dots, \rho_k$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ into $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{C})$ that are pairwise inequivalent.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is no function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with the following property: for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, every group $G$ whose $k$-th derived subgroup $G^{(k)}$ is trivial, and every generating set $A$ of $G$, if $x^4 = 1$ for every element $x$ of every subgroup generated by a finite subset of $A$ with at most $f(k)$ elements, then $x^4 = 1$ for every $x \in G$. This is the negative answer to Kourovka…

results.title: G-harmonic tuples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers. The tuple $a$ is $G$-harmonic if every $a_i$ is positive and there exist subgroups $U_1, \dots, U_n$ of $G$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $U_i$ has index $a_i$ in $G$ for every $i$ and the left cosets $g_1 U_1, \dots, g_n U_n$ are pairwise disjoint.

results.title: Constructing a G-harmonic tuple
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers with every $a_i$ positive. If $U_1, \dots, U_n$ are subgroups of $G$ such that $U_i$ has index $a_i$ in $G$ for every $i$, and $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ are elements such that the left cosets $g_1 U_1, \dots, g_n U_n$ are pairwise disjoint, then $a$ is $G$-harmonic.

results.title: Entries of a G-harmonic tuple are positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group. If a tuple $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of natural numbers is $G$-harmonic, then $a_i > 0$ for every $i$.

results.title: Witnesses for a G-harmonic tuple
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group. If a tuple $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of natural numbers is $G$-harmonic, then there exist subgroups $U_1, \dots, U_n$ of $G$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $U_i$ has index $a_i$ in $G$ for every $i$ and the left cosets $g_1 U_1, \dots, g_n U_n$ are pairwise disjoint.

results.title: Characterization of G-harmonic tuples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers. Then $a$ is $G$-harmonic if and only if every $a_i$ is positive and there are subgroups $U_1, \dots, U_n$ of $G$ and elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ such that $U_i$ has index $a_i$ in $G$ for every $i$ and the left cosets $g_1 U_1, \dots, g_n U_n$ are pairwise disjoint.

results.title: The empty tuple is G-harmonic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group $G$, the empty tuple of natural numbers is (vacuously) $G$-harmonic.

results.title: The tuple (1) is G-harmonic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group $G$, the one-entry tuple $(1)$ is $G$-harmonic; the subgroup $G$ itself, of index $1$, with coset representative $1$ witnesses this.

results.title: Tuples with a zero entry are not G-harmonic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group. If a tuple $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ of natural numbers has $a_i = 0$ for some $i$, then $a$ is not $G$-harmonic.

results.title: Two distinct lines meet in their cross product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $v \ne w$ be two distinct points of the projective plane $\mathbb{P}(K^3)$. Call two points orthogonal when the dot product of representative vectors in $K^3$ vanishes, and let $v \times w$ be the point spanned by the cross product of representatives of $v$ and $w$, which is nonzero since $v \ne w$. Then a point $p$ equals $v \times w$ if and only if $p$ is orthogonal to both $v$ and $w$.…

results.title: Line arrangement
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A line arrangement in the projective plane over a field $K$ is a finite set of at least two lines, each line recorded by its coordinate vector, a point of the dual projective plane $\mathbb{P}(K^3)$.

results.title: Multiplicity of a point in a line arrangement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. The multiplicity $m_p$ of a point $p$ in $A$ is the number of lines of $A$ through $p$, that is, of lines of $A$ whose coordinate vector has zero dot product with a representative of $p$.

results.title: Singular points of a line arrangement
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The singular points of a line arrangement $A$ in the projective plane over a field form the finite set of intersection points of pairs of distinct lines of $A$, where two distinct lines with coordinate vectors $\ell$ and $\ell'$ meet in the point spanned by the cross product $\ell \times \ell'$ of their representatives.

results.title: Singular points lie on two distinct lines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. A point $p$ is a singular point of $A$ if and only if there are two distinct lines of $A$ that both pass through $p$.

results.title: Singular points are the points of multiplicity at least two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. A point $p$ is a singular point of $A$ if and only if its multiplicity $m_p$ in $A$, the number of lines of $A$ through $p$, satisfies $m_p \ge 2$.

results.title: Multiplicity is at most the number of lines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the projective plane over a field. Every point $p$ has multiplicity $m_p \le d$ in $A$.

results.title: Every line arrangement has a singular point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every line arrangement in the projective plane over a field has at least one singular point, since any two of its distinct lines meet.

results.title: Harbourne constant of a line arrangement

results.summary: Let $A$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the projective plane over a field, let $S$ be its set of singular points, with $s$ elements, and let $m_p$ be the multiplicity of a point $p$ in $A$. The Harbourne constant of $A$ is the real number

results.title: Inf-sup condition
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The inf–sup condition: there is `β > 0` such that `β * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖B x‖` for every `x`. The right-hand side is the dual norm of the functional `B x`, i.e. `sup_{‖y‖ ≤ 1} |B x y|` (see `norm_apply_eq_iSup`).

results.title: Nondegeneracy in the second variable
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The only `y` annihilated by every `B x` is `y = 0`.

results.title: Dual norm as a supremum over the unit ball
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The dual norm is the supremum over the closed unit ball.

results.title: Inf-sup condition in supremum form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inf–sup condition in classical supremum form.

results.title: Operator associated to a bounded bilinear form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The operator `E →L[ℝ] F` associated to a bounded bilinear form `B : E →L[ℝ] F →L[ℝ] ℝ`, characterized by `⟪bilinearFormSharp B x, y⟫ = B x y`. This is the two-space analogue of Mathlib's `continuousLinearMapOfBilin` (which is stated for `E = F`).

results.title: Inf-sup condition makes the associated operator antilipschitz
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inf–sup condition makes `bilinearFormSharp B` antilipschitz.

results.title: Inf-sup condition makes the associated operator injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inf–sup condition makes `bilinearFormSharp B` injective.

results.title: Inf-sup condition makes the associated operator's range closed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inf–sup condition makes the range of `bilinearFormSharp B` closed.

results.title: Inf-sup and nondegeneracy make the associated operator surjective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inf–sup condition plus nondegeneracy make `bilinearFormSharp B` surjective: the orthogonal complement of its range is trivial, and a closed subspace of a Hilbert space with trivial orthogonal complement is everything.

results.title: Banach–Nečas–Babuška isomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Banach–Nečas–Babuška isomorphism: the operator associated to a bilinear form satisfying the inf–sup condition and nondegeneracy is a continuous linear equivalence.

results.title: Banach–Nečas–Babuška isomorphism is characterized by the form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The equivalence `sharpEquiv` is characterized by the bilinear form.

results.title: Norm of the Banach–Nečas–Babuška isomorphism applied to a vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The norm of `sharpEquiv` applied to `x` is the dual norm of `B x`.

results.title: Pointwise inverse bound for the Banach–Nečas–Babuška isomorphism
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pointwise inverse bound for `sharpEquiv`: the inverse operator is bounded by `β⁻¹` when `β` is an inf–sup constant.

results.title: Operator-norm bound for the inverse Banach–Nečas–Babuška isomorphism
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Operator-norm bound for the inverse: `‖(sharpEquiv)⁻¹‖ ≤ β⁻¹`.

results.title: Banach–Nečas–Babuška theorem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Banach–Nečas–Babuška theorem: a bilinear form satisfying the inf–sup condition and nondegeneracy is itself a continuous linear equivalence `E ≃L[ℝ] (F →L[ℝ] ℝ)`.

results.title: Banach–Nečas–Babuška equivalence acts as the bilinear form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The equivalence `continuousLinearEquivOfBilinearForm` acts as `B`.

results.title: Unique solvability of the inf-sup variational problem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The variational problem `B x y = φ y` for all `y` has a unique solution.

results.title: Stability bound for the inf-sup variational problem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The variational problem has a solution with the stability bound `‖x‖ ≤ β⁻¹ * ‖φ‖`.

results.title: Couplings
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be measurable spaces, $P$ a measure on $X$ and $Q$ a measure on $Y$. A coupling of $P$ and $Q$ is a probability measure $\pi$ on $X \times Y$ whose marginals are $P$ and $Q$: the pushforward of $\pi$ under the projection $X \times Y \to X$ is $P$, and its pushforward under the projection $X \times Y \to Y$ is $Q$. The set of couplings is written $\Pi(P, Q)$.

results.title: Kantorovich cost
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be measurable spaces and $c \colon X \times Y \to [0, \infty]$ a cost function. The Kantorovich cost of a measure $\pi$ on $X \times Y$ is $I(\pi) = \int_{X \times Y} c \, d\pi \in [0, \infty]$, the Lebesgue integral of $c$ against $\pi$ (for a non-measurable $c$, the lower Lebesgue integral).

results.title: The polynomial $\operatorname{per}(A + xJ)$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real $n \times n$ matrix $A$, this is the polynomial $\operatorname{per}(A + xJ) \in \mathbb{R}[x]$, where $J$ is the $n \times n$ all-ones matrix: the permanent of the $n \times n$ matrix of polynomials whose $(i, j)$ entry is $A_{ij} + x$.

results.title: The Haglund–Ono–Wagner monotone column permanent conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the statement that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every real $n \times n$ matrix $A$ whose columns are weakly increasing ($A_{ij} \le A_{i'j}$ whenever $i \le i'$), every complex root of the polynomial $\operatorname{per}(A + xJ) \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ is real, where $J$ is the $n \times n$ all-ones matrix.

results.title: Brändén–Haglund–Visontai–Wagner theorem (monotone column permanent conjecture)

results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every real $n \times n$ matrix $A$ whose columns are weakly increasing ($A_{ij} \le A_{i'j}$ whenever $i \le i'$), every complex root of the polynomial $\operatorname{per}(A + xJ) \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ is real, where $J$ is the $n \times n$ all-ones matrix.

results.title: Counter-machine instructions
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A counter-machine instruction is one of: increment register $r$, decrement register $r$, or jump to instruction $q$ if register $r$ is zero, where the register index $r$ and the jump target $q$ are natural numbers.

results.title: Counter-machine states
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A counter-machine state consists of a program counter, which is a natural number, and the register contents, a function assigning a natural number to every register index $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: One step of a counter machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p$ be a counter-machine program, a list of instructions indexed from $0$, and let $s$ be a state with program counter $c$. If $c$ is at least the length of $p$ (the machine has halted), the step leaves $s$ unchanged. Otherwise it executes instruction $c$ of $p$: increment register $r$ adds $1$ to register $r$ and sets the program counter to $c + 1$; decrement register $r$ subtracts $1$ from register $r$ if it…

results.title: Initial state of a counter machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The initial counter-machine state on a list of inputs $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ has program counter $0$, register $i$ holding $x_i$ for each $i < k$, and every other register holding $0$.

results.title: Bounded execution of a counter machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a counter-machine program $p$, a natural number $t$ and a state $s$, the execution of $p$ for $t$ steps from $s$ is the state obtained from $s$ by applying $t$ single steps of $p$.

results.title: Output of a counter machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The output of a counter-machine program $p$ on a list of inputs is the partial natural number obtained as follows: run $p$ from the initial state on those inputs; if for some number $t$ of steps the program counter is at least the length of $p$ (the machine has halted), the output is the content of register $0$ after the least such $t$; if no such $t$ exists, the output is undefined.

results.title: A counter step is sticky at halting states
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Past the end of the program the state does not change.

results.title: Counter-machine execution is stable once halted
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a counter-machine program, $s$ a state and $t$ a natural number. If the state reached from $s$ after $t$ steps of $p$ has program counter at least the length of $p$, then the state reached from $s$ after $t + 1$ steps equals the state reached after $t$ steps.

results.title: Counter-machine execution is constant after halting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a counter-machine program, $s$ a state, and $t_1 \le t_2$ natural numbers. If the state reached from $s$ after $t_1$ steps of $p$ has program counter at least the length of $p$, then the state reached from $s$ after $t_2$ steps equals the state reached after $t_1$ steps.

results.title: Output membership for counter machines
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a counter-machine program, let $x$ be a list of natural-number inputs, and let $t$ and $y$ be natural numbers. If the state reached after $t$ steps of $P$ from the initial state on $x$ has program counter at least the length of $P$ (so the machine has halted) and register $0$ holds $y$ in that state, then the output of $P$ on $x$ is defined and equals $y$.

results.title: Counter-machine decidable predicates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is counter-machine decidable when some counter-machine program computes its characteristic function: for every natural number $n$, the output of the program on the single input $n$ is defined and equals $1$ if $P(n)$ holds and $0$ otherwise.
